env: A 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell host with Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and populated `NGC_CLI_API_KEY` for NGC image/model pulls. The VSS repository is checked out at `{{repo_root}}`. This runtime eval verifies that `vss-build-vision-agent` can generate and deploy an LVS summarization add-on profile, upload or use a VIOS-stored warehouse video, call the generated LVS REST API at `POST /v1/summarize`, and return actual summary data from `choices[0].message.content`. Use the local RT-VLM in-process backend plus a local Nemotron LLM NIM on the 2-GPU host to avoid depending on external remote inference endpoints. For deterministic eval choices, use build directory `{{repo_root}}/_builds/an-1-runtime/`, compose profile flag `bp_developer_an_1_runtime`, and local Nemotron service key `nvidia-nemotron-nano-9b-v2` when the skill asks for explicit build, profile, or local LLM placement decisions. Use an existing warehouse MP4 from the repository sample-data tree or the eval host sample-data directories, preferring `warehouse_safety_0001.mp4` when present, and record the path used. Live streaming video summarization is intentionally out of scope: do not emit the NvStreamer validation harness and do not use `/v1/stream_summarize` or `/v1/generate_captions` as the summarization output path.

expects.query: Can you use `/vss-build-vision-agent` to add video summarization to an existing VSS profile? The videos should be uploaded to or stored through the VIOS recorder, not live streams. Please generate the build under `_builds/an-1-runtime`, deploy it locally, reuse the existing VIOS, RT-VLM, Kafka, Logstash, and Elasticsearch stack instead of duplicating infrastructure, and add the LVS server with a local Nemotron LLM if needed. After it is running, use a warehouse sample video from VIOS storage, call `POST /v1/summarize` exactly once with scenario `warehouse monitoring` and events `["boxes falling", "forklift stuck", "person entering restricted area"]`, then show the returned `video_summary` and every event from `choices[0].message.content`. Leave the deployment running so I can inspect it.
checks: `{{repo_root}}/_builds/an-1-runtime/compose.yml`, `.env`, `.env.template`, `MANIFEST.md`, and `allow-list.yml` exist in the same generated build folder.

`{{repo_root}}/_builds/an-1-runtime/allow-list.yml` includes the exact LVS service key `lvs-server` from `services/video-summarization/compose.yml`, includes/reuses the required peer component sets for VIOS, RT-VLM, Kafka, Logstash, and Elasticsearch, includes exactly one selected local Nemotron LLM key (`nvidia-nemotron-nano-9b-v2`), and does not define duplicate Kafka or Elasticsearch stacks.

The generated sidecar does NOT contain a `validation_harness:` key and the generated compose does NOT include `vss-vios-nvstreamer` or an `nvstreamer-validation` service, because this runtime eval covers stored/uploaded video summarization rather than live streaming video summarization.

`docker compose --env-file .env -f compose.yml --profile bp_developer_an_1_runtime config` from `{{repo_root}}/_builds/an-1-runtime/` returns exit 0 with zero real unexpanded `${...}` tokens other than intentional shell escapes or `${VAR:-default}` consumer-side defaults.

The generated deployment is actually running: `docker ps` shows the key long-running containers for Kafka, Elasticsearch, Logstash, VIOS (`vss-vios-ingress`, `vss-vios-sensor`, and `vss-vios-streamprocessing` or their generated equivalents), RT-VLM (`vss-rtvi-vlm`), the selected Nemotron LLM NIM (`nvidia-nemotron-nano-9b-v2`), and LVS (`vss-lvs`). Any exited one-shot init containers in the generated stack have exit code 0.

Runtime health probes pass: `curl -sf http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health` returns Elasticsearch status `yellow` or `green`; `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns exit 0 for VIOS; `curl -sf http://localhost:8018/v1/health/ready` returns exit 0 for RT-VLM; `curl -sf http://localhost:30081/v1/models` returns a non-empty LLM model list; `curl -sf http://localhost:38111/v1/ready` returns exit 0 for LVS; and `curl -sf http://localhost:38111/models` returns a non-empty model list containing the id used in the summarize request.

A warehouse video is actually available through VIOS storage: after upload or selecting an existing VIOS-stored copy, VIOS `sensor/list` and `sensor/<sensorId>/streams` expose a stream id, and a VIOS snapshot or clip endpoint returns HTTP 200 with non-empty image or MP4 bytes.

The agent obtains a temporary MP4 clip URL through the VIOS storage API (`/storage/file/<streamId>/url` with `container=mp4`, response field `.videoUrl`) or an equivalent VIOS-provided URL/id that `lvs-server` can fetch. The URL/id used in the summarize request must be derived from VIOS, not fabricated.

The agent issues exactly one `POST http://localhost:38111/v1/summarize` or `POST http://${HOST_IP}:38111/v1/summarize` call after LVS is ready and after the VIOS clip URL/id is available. The request body is JSON and contains `model`, `scenario`, `events`, `chunk_duration`, `num_frames_per_second_or_fixed_frames_chunk`, `use_fps_for_chunking`, and either `url` or `id`; `scenario` equals `warehouse monitoring` and `events` equals `["boxes falling", "forklift stuck", "person entering restricted area"]`.

The video summarization response is HTTP 200 and the body is an OpenAI-style envelope with `choices[0].message.content` populated as a non-empty string. This check requires the actual LVS API response; documentation-only or dry-run output is insufficient.

Parsing `choices[0].message.content` as JSON yields an object with a non-empty `video_summary` field and a non-empty `events` array. Every returned event has at least `start_time`, `end_time`, `type`, and `description` or semantically equivalent event fields.

The agent's final response renders the actual `video_summary` from the LVS response and includes every returned event description. A response that only says the API call succeeded, or only reports status/health, fails this check.

The agent never uses `/v1/stream_summarize` or `/v1/generate_captions` as the summarization output path for this eval, and never calls a VLM `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint directly for summarization. All summarization traffic goes through the generated LVS service at `/v1/summarize`.
No upstream compose or config file under `{{repo_root}}/deploy/docker/` was modified by generation or deployment; `git diff --quiet HEAD -- deploy/docker/` returns exit 0 at the end of the run.
